recent_posts.title: How Yelp Keeps Server-Driven UI Consistent Across Four Platforms
recent_posts.summary: Yelp's engineering team explains how they extended their CHAOS server-driven UI framework to integrate with Cookbook, their cross-platform design system, using an auto-generated bridge library called Konbini. A single JSON interface definition for each component automatically generates four platform-specific libraries (Python for backend, Kotlin for Android, Swift for iOS, TypeScript/React for Web), ensuring consistent serialization and deserialization across all clients. The post covers how tokens (colors, icons, etc.) are handled, and how a versioning and migration system ensures backward compatibility when component interfaces change — allowing older app versions to continue working as components evolve.

recent_posts.title: Zero downtime Upgrade: Yelp’s Cassandra 4.x Upgrade Story
recent_posts.summary: Yelp's Database Reliability Engineering team upgraded over a thousand Cassandra nodes from version 3.11 to 4.1 with zero downtime. The post covers their upgrade strategy including benchmarking (4% p99 latency improvement, 11% throughput gain, up to 58% p99 reduction on key clusters), compatibility challenges with Stargate proxy and Cassandra Source Connector, and a three-stage automated upgrade process (pre-flight, flight, post-flight). Key lessons include a Stargate 2.x regression causing slower range queries (resolved by downgrading to 1.x), schema disagreement on CDC-enabled clusters, and the value of running version-specific components in parallel during the transition. The upgrade was performed in-place via rolling restart on Kubernetes, avoiding the cost and complexity of a separate DC approach.

recent_posts.title: Building Biz Ask Anything: From Prototype to Product
recent_posts.summary: Yelp's engineering team details how they evolved 'Biz Ask Anything' (Yelp Assistant on business pages) from a two-week prototype to a production system over nine months. Key challenges covered include: building near-real-time data pipelines (NRT indices, Cassandra EAV store) with sub-100ms reads; a multi-stage question analysis pipeline with fine-tuned GPT-4.1-nano models for Trust & Safety classification, inquiry type routing, content source selection, and keyword generation; multi-dimensional answer quality evaluation using LLM-as-judge graders (correctness, completeness, evidence relevance); latency reduction from 10-20s to under 3s p75 via streaming (SSE), async pipelines, and model prioritization; cost reduction to 25% of original via smaller fine-tuned models, intelligent context window trimming, and dynamic prompt composition; and content-driven suggested questions that lifted engagement ~50% and reduced inability-to-answer rate by ~26%.

recent_posts.title: How Yelp Built a Back-Testing Engine for Safer, Smarter Ad Budget Allocation
recent_posts.summary: Yelp developed a back-testing engine to safely simulate changes to their ad budget allocation system before deploying them to production. The system replays historical campaign data day-by-day using production code, ML models (CatBoost) to predict outcomes like clicks and leads, and Bayesian optimization (Scikit-Optimize) to explore parameter spaces. This approach allows faster iteration, reduces A/B testing risks, catches bugs early, and provides more accurate impact predictions than traditional methods. The engine integrates eight components including Git submodules for production code, Redshift for historical data, and MLFlow for experiment tracking.

recent_posts.title: S3 server access logs at scale
recent_posts.summary: Yelp's infrastructure team built a scalable system to process terabytes of S3 server access logs daily, converting raw logs to Parquet format to reduce storage by 85% and object count by 99.99%. The solution uses AWS Athena for querying, partition projection for efficient data access, and S3 batch operations for lifecycle management. The system enables debugging access issues, cost attribution, incident response, and data retention decisions by identifying unused objects through joining S3 inventory with access logs. Key challenges included handling malformed logs with user-controlled fields, managing Athena query limits, and ensuring idempotent insertions across distributed systems.

recent_posts.title: Exploring CHAOS: Building a Backend for Server-Driven UI
recent_posts.summary: Yelp's CHAOS framework enables server-driven UI by using a GraphQL API that routes requests to backend services which construct UI configurations. The system uses Python dataclasses to define reusable components and actions, supports parallel feature loading for performance, includes error handling to prevent single feature failures from breaking entire views, and offers advanced features like view flows for navigation sequences and view placeholders for asynchronous content loading.

recent_posts.title: Revenue Automation Series: Testing an Integration with Third-Party System
recent_posts.summary: Yelp's engineering team developed a comprehensive testing strategy for their revenue data pipeline integration with third-party systems. They implemented a staging pipeline approach to eliminate 10-hour data verification delays, created automated data integrity checkers to ensure 99.99% accuracy, and established robust validation processes for external system uploads. The solution includes parallel pipeline testing, automated schema validation, and both REST API and SFTP upload methods, significantly improving testing efficiency and reducing manual verification errors.

recent_posts.title: Nrtsearch 1.0.0: Incremental Backups, Lucene 10, and More
recent_posts.summary: Nrtsearch 1.0.0 has been released, featuring major enhancements such as incremental backups to S3 on every commit and switching architecture to use ephemeral local disks instead of EBS volumes, improving replica startup speed and reliability. The release also updates Nrtsearch to Lucene 10 for improved performance and features like vector search using the HNSW algorithm. A redevelopment of state management has made state updates more durable and efficient. New functionality includes advanced vector search capabilities, integration of an aggregation system with parallel search, and extensive plugin support for customized search operations.

recent_posts.title: Journey to Zero Trust Access
recent_posts.summary: Yelp implemented a Zero Trust Access strategy to support its fully remote workforce, replacing its legacy VPN with Netbird, supported by WireGuard. The transition aimed to improve security, user experience, and throughput while reducing VPN usage for general connectivity needs. The solution includes OpenID Connect integration with Okta, high performance, and fault tolerance. Yelp customized Netbird to enhance usability and ensure quick self-repair options for users, contributing open-source improvements back to the community.

recent_posts.title: Revenue Automation Series: Building Revenue Data Pipeline
recent_posts.summary: Yelp faced challenges in automating their revenue recognition process due to the complexity of revenue streams and manual operations. They developed a data pipeline using a Revenue Recognition SaaS solution (REVREC), integrating Yelp’s data with a standardized ETL architecture. The process included handling ambiguous requirements, performing data gap analysis, and evaluating system designs. Ultimately, Yelp chose a Data Lake + Spark ETL approach and utilized internal tools to manage the ETL pipeline, address technical challenges, and streamline debugging. Future improvements include enhanced data interfaces, simplified data models, and unified implementation standards.

top_posts.title: Loading data into Redshift with DBT
top_posts.summary: At Yelp, using DBT with Redshift Spectrum has streamlined the process of loading data into Redshift, improving performance, schema management, and data consistency. This new approach has reduced runtime from hours to minutes and eliminated delays. Improvements include simplified schema changes, automated backfills, and better data deduplication, providing significant benefits across multiple datasets.

top_posts.title: Migrating in-place from PostgreSQL to MySQL
top_posts.summary: The Yelp Reservations service, originally built with a PostgreSQL database, faced maintenance and outage response issues due to limited expertise. To alleviate these issues, Yelp migrated to a MySQL database. The project involved extensive modifications to handle PostgreSQL-specific features like array columns and triggers. For ensuring data integrity and consistency during the transition, both databases were kept in sync, and reads were gradually switched to MySQL. The release was executed over several months to minimize disruptions and ensure data accuracy.

top_posts.title: dbt Generic Tests in Sessions Validation at Yelp
top_posts.summary: Yelp's Clickstream Analytics team uses dbt for sessions data mart validation, enhancing data quality and easing the development cycle. Challenges such as managing validation queries and sharing results are alleviated by dbt’s ability to persist version-controlled queries and execute them across various data stores. dbt generic tests ensure data integrity, offer customization, and leverage tags for effective test management. The approach accelerates development while ensuring the swift delivery of validated data to production.

top_posts.title: Boosting ML Pipeline Efficiency: Direct Cassandra Ingestion from Spark
top_posts.summary: Yelp enhanced their Machine Learning platform by enabling direct data ingestion from Spark to Cassandra, which streamlined their feature publication process. This improvement resulted in significant infrastructure cost savings, better developer efficiency, and enhanced data availability. Key changes included disabling batch mode for writes, limiting concurrent writers, and employing static rate-limiting and Zookeeper for concurrency control.
